title: A loop that lost a push race lands on its Turn

statements.says: A loop that loses a push race waits for its Turn, the right to push to main that one loop in a clone holds at a time, and keeps it until it Lands.
Every push takes the Turn.
A loop that has not lost holds the Turn for a few seconds, only for its push.
A loop that lost holds the Turn from fetch to push, with the Suite inside, so the loops beside it wait at their push and cannot beat it again.
A lost push race is tried again for as long as it takes.
A loop that waits for the Turn says which spec and ticket hold it.
The Turn is let go when the loop that held it ends, however it ends.
Any push error other than a lost race stops the loop at once.
Another loop pushing is an expected event and not a failure.
The logs proved that a bounded retry did not answer a lost push.
A lost push costs a whole Suite run, 13 to 34 minutes here, and one loop landed inside that window every time.
Two landings each rebased three times, passed the Suite three times, lost three times and stopped their loops.
Not one landing across the repository's loop logs met a conflict, so the time went on Suite runs and never on fixing anything.
A waiting loop names the spec and ticket holding the Turn so that a Suite that hangs inside a landing is found.
A push error other than a lost race stops the loop because a person has to fix it.
Holding the Turn for every landing was rejected, because a loop with no race to lose would wait on a loop that lost, and most landings meet no race.
Letting a loop that has not lost push without the Turn was rejected, because it pushes while the holder runs its Suite and the holder loses again.
One lander that takes tickets from a queue was rejected, because the next ticket of a spec often needs the one before it on main, so the loop waits all the same.
Skipping the Suite after a clean rebase was rejected, because a rebase with no conflict can still break the program.
A GitHub merge queue was rejected, because it needs pull requests and this repository has none.
A Turn that every clone shares was rejected, because the races seen were between loops of one clone, and the retry still lands work that a push from somewhere else beat.
It replaces the earlier decision that rejected holding a lock across landing and relied on a bounded retry for a lost push.
